reason: Absence ratchet: geometric comparison reconstructs all wall corners in file coordinates and compares their polygon up to cyclic start and reversed walk, with the run treated as an unoriented line. Dimensions, depth/across directions and every corner coordinate must agree.

The run's sense is chosen by its coordinates in the frame, and one of them is zero up to round-off (mfcadpp/10155: run (0, 0.3147, -0.9492) in the frame; nist_ctc_04: (0, 0.3206, -0.9472)), so the placement's round-off decides it; the same line (and wall outline, listed from the other end). Schema 6 renames this publication family (for #92); the recogniser and comparison floor are unchanged. Resolved by the schema-6 run-to-axis mapping: the existing geometric comparator canonicalises the axis line sense, so these two sign-only differences disappear. The zero allowance is an absence ratchet; recognisers and geometry are unchanged.
The same prism; the ring's first side is chosen by coordinates in the frame where two sides tie up to round-off, so flat_directions and flat_centres are listed from another side.

Equivalent: only the flat pattern's triangulation of three flat faces differs (vertices by up to 0.04 mm, and the triangles over them): the kernel's plane triangulation keeps different boundary samples under this rotation; the development itself is the same. The translate, rot_zx_moved and caller_space differences were thinning choosing between equally far samples by round-off (crates/haecceity/src/cloud.rs now breaks that tie), and are gone; what still differs here under the generic rotation is undetermined. The fingerprint ignores flat_pattern for this reason.

For #92 the document motion test now compares every file-coordinate measurement instead of comparing formerly local fields only in their recognition frames. Face [0] has an Axial frame gauge: roll about the turning axis is unconstrained. The two valid frame representatives choose different transverse height directions for the cylindrical riser. Its explicitly published height and other axes therefore describe different support planes of the same face. Frame voting, face identity and intrinsic fingerprints are unchanged; this height-context ambiguity requires the deferred recognition-frame work, not a publication exception. The vector publication tests independently check scalar extrema against the defining face.
